description: Some nodes cannot reach others; from the inside it looks exactly like those nodes crashed.
Every operation appears to happen at one instant between its start and end, so an acknowledged write is seen by every later read on any node.
During a partition, a replicated system must choose between consistency (linearizability) and availability (every live node answers).
A CP system rejects requests on the side without a majority; an AP system keeps answering on both sides and reconciles conflicts later.
If partitioned, choose availability or consistency; else, choose latency or consistency, because coordination costs round trips.
With N replicas, waiting for W write acknowledgements and R read replies makes every read overlap the latest acknowledged write when R + W > N.
